newsitem.title: FRANCE: France, Cuba said to renew grain-sugar barter deal.
newsitem.headline: France, Cuba said to renew grain-sugar barter deal.

text.p: France and Cuba have agreed to renew an annual food-for-sugar barter deal through 1997, French banking sources said on Wednesday.
Last week's unannounced agreement, guaranteed by a Coface export credit, is valued at some $175 million, they said. A similar agreement last year was worth $155 million.
The deal traditionally renewed at this time of year involves the supply of wheat to Cuba but also includes equipment parts and farm machinery.
In return, Cuba supplies French traders with sugar for onward sale to the world market.
France is the main exporter of wheat to Cuba, followed by Canada, because of a 36-year-old U.S. embargo against the Communist-ruled Caribbean island.
France sold close to 500,000 tonnes of soft wheat to Cuba in the 1995/96 (July/June) campaign and 800,000 tonnes in 1994/95. --Paris newsroom +331 4221 5432
